To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified two QTLs in S. pennellii for enhanced fruit quality and have successfully introgressed these QTLs into cultivated varieties.
The introgressed lines IL7-3 and 12-4 harbour QTL that increase the content in tomato fruit of ascorbic and phenolic compounds and of soluble solids, respectively.
the introgression of two S. pennellii QTL into the M82 tomato variety increased the content of antioxidant molecules (AsA, total phenol) and °Bx in tomato fruit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new sources of variation for fruit quality traits, and with their use in breeding programmes for tomato improvement.
the identification of favourable alleles and their pyramiding into elite tomato varieties, in order to increase the content of antioxidant compounds and °Bx in tomato fruit.
the development of a novel tomato variety with enhanced antioxidant content.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present work represents a significant step towards the identification and characterization of QTLs for antioxidant content and °Bx, and the development of new tomato varieties with increased fruit quality.

the two introgression lines IL7-3 and 12-4 harbouring QTL that increase AsA and phenolic content and °Bx in tomato fruit were pyramided into cultivated tomato varieties and their progenies displayed a significant increase of AsA, total soluble phenols and ° Bx.

the two QTLs for AsA, total and soluble phenols and °Brx were successfully pyramided into a single tomato genotype, and that the pyramided QTLs are stable and can be used to breed new varieties with enhanced nutritional quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
QTL pyramiding is an effective strategy to improve the genetic basis for fruit quality traits.
we identified two QTL in S. pennellii and that we pyramided them to increase the content of AsA, phenols and °brix.
the introgressions from S. pennellii can be combined into a single genotype to increase AsA, phenols and ° Bx content in tomato fruit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the introgression of two QTLs, each of them contributing to different antioxidant traits, was possible without any detrimental effects on the agronomic performance of the plants.
the introgression of multiple QTL for fruit quality traits can be successfully achieved in tomato.
the introgression lines IL7-3+IL12-4 represent a new genetic resource that may help tomato breeders to develop new cultivars with enhanced fruit antioxidant content.
